    How books are judged

    The collection separates eligibility, vetoes and quality. A high score cannot override an exclusion or a veto. The Books view includes every eligible, non-vetoed source work, including poor fits.

    SourcesHard exclusionsVetoesScoringEvidence and uncertaintyDomains and connectionsSite controlsExact rules

    1. Collect and identify source books

    Read the submitted page, its main content, comments and replies. Expand comments where access permits, and record missing or inaccessible material. Only books named or directly linked in that source become candidates. External research can establish identity and evidence; it does not add unrelated titles.

    Resolve author, title, aliases, editions and nominated scope. A whole series and one volume are different scopes. Merge duplicate mentions of the same work and retain every distinct numbered source. Repeated mentions are not independent evidence of quality. Ambiguous identities remain in the source audit until resolved.

    For an existing work, read its prior assessments and reassess the gates, all criteria, deductions, dates and confidence using old and new evidence. Explain what changed or remained. Update its existing entry; preserve prior analyses as history. A work belongs to at most one of the recommended, vetoed and excluded lists.

    Books Guru batch exception, 21 October 2026. The user expressly requested documentation without deeper analysis for titles covered by any earlier source. These 26 lists therefore retain existing assessments and add source provenance only. Duplicate titles, aliases and previously covered series members are documented; only unique new works receive new gate and score assessments. This exception does not change the normal reassessment rule.

    2. Apply hard exclusions first

    1. Book form — current rule. Works which do not represent a book and are never published in a book form. Non-book references stay outside all three book ledgers.
    2. Fiction — current rule. Exclude fiction books and do not consider them vetoed. Discard them before scoring or further analysis.
    3. H3 — Technical training and reference exclusion — current rule. Technical training and reference exclusion. Exclude works whose main purpose is to teach a technical curriculum, develop specialist proficiency, present formal proofs or derivations, provide procedures, or serve as a technical reference. Clear prose, historical introductions, conceptual explanations, prestige, and absence of exercises do not override this exclusion. Allow technically demanding books when their main purpose is sustained explanation of discoveries, mechanisms, decisions, or historical development, and their main intellectual value can be obtained without completing a course of technical study. Historical scientific treatises remain excluded when their main content requires reconstruction of specialist proofs, notation, or obsolete technical methods. Historical importance alone does not establish eligibility. Historical surveys and annotated chronologies can qualify when substantive explanatory prose provides value beyond locating references.

    Assess the main purpose and the work required of its reader. Clear prose, historical introductions and conceptual explanations do not admit a technical curriculum, proof collection or specialist reference. Historical surveys and annotated chronologies can qualify when their explanatory prose has value beyond locating references. Difficulty or classroom adoption alone does not exclude a genuinely explanatory history.

    Investigate uncertain cases rather than classify from a title. Hard-excluded books receive neither ordinary nor counterfactual scores. The biography exceptions below cannot override these exclusions. Earlier analyses preserve the rules and judgments used at their dates; the latest rule review determines current membership.

    3. Check vetoes

    After hard exclusions, a veto applies when one of these conditions is present at a serious level:

    1. V1 — Epistemic failure. The central argument depends on material factual errors, distorted sources, invalid causal inference, concealed uncertainty or obsolete information presented as current.
    2. V2 — Ideological capture. Allegiance replaces evidence; counterexamples are ignored, caricatured or treated asymmetrically.
    3. V3 — No transferable intellectual payload. Little mechanism, constraint, model, heuristic or general lesson survives removal of local detail. Mathematical, scientific and high-tech biographies or memoirs have the specified exception.
    4. V4 — Hype or ephemerality dependence — current rule. Hype or ephemerality dependence - The book’s value depends primarily on a passing controversy, fashionable terminology, launch publicity, or premature claims of revolutionary importance. Educated speculative prediction is allowed if stated in professional substantiated balanced argumentative way with elaborate guardrails.
    5. V5 — Religious doctrine or ideological extremism — current rule. Religious doctrine or ideological extremism. Veto scripture, devotional or proselytizing works, and works whose central purpose is to establish religious doctrine as authoritative truth. Also veto explicit advocacy of ideological extremism, supported by specific evidence such as dehumanization, persecution, violent domination or suppression of dissent. A manifesto label, advocacy, activism, political position, technological vision, institutional criticism or proposed reform is not sufficient. Historical or analytical discussion of religion or extremist movements is not itself advocacy.
    6. V6 — Partisan mobilization — current rule. Partisan mobilization. Veto works whose dominant purpose is to recruit, rally, or reinforce allegiance to a political leader, party, or movement, or to supply campaign attacks against opponents. Establish this purpose from the introduction, representative passages, and stated aims. Apply the rule equally across political positions. A policy conclusion, institutional criticism, or reform proposal alone is insufficient.

    For V4, inspect the evidence, assumptions, uncertainty, failure conditions and counterarguments. A forecast or speculative topic alone is insufficient; expert standing alone also does not establish the required safeguards. For V5, identify a central doctrinal purpose or specific advocacy of extremism. A manifesto label, activism, institutional criticism, technological vision or proposed reform does not establish either condition. Discussion of religion or extremism is not itself endorsement.

    Apply each veto independently and record the serious defect and supporting evidence. Do not replace a withdrawn V4 or V5 with V1 or V2 merely because a book takes a position. Retain another veto only when its own test is supported.

    V6 separately tests dominant recruitment, allegiance-building and campaign attacks, across political positions. A book can pass V5 and still fail V6. A policy conclusion, institutional criticism or reform proposal alone is insufficient. The October 2026 category review applies revised H3 and V6 while preserving existing numerical assessments; two previously unscored works admitted under H3 receive their first baseline assessments.

    Record the rule, reason and confidence. A low score or weak topic fit is not another veto. Each vetoed work retains a full counterfactual assessment: suspend only the veto gate, keep the identified flaws and deductions, and calculate its score. That score does not make it recommended. The Vetoed view displays this saved score, unaffected by custom settings.

    4. Assess ten positive criteria

    The profile favors pragmatic explanation of how science, technology, production, logistics, energy, trade, finance, institutions and strategic power interact. It assumes a reader trained in theoretical physics, computation and numerical simulation. Popular exposition can therefore have strong factual quality but low additional utility for this reader.

    Assess a linear attainment x between zero and each criterion's own maximum m. The ten maxima sum to 100. Only evidence, systems integration and information density use a quadratic profile.

    CriterionMaximumProfileWhat is assessed
    Evidence and inferential integrity20QuadraticReliable facts, sources, inference, uncertainty, and counterevidence.
    Systems integration17QuadraticCoherent connections between relevant layers of a system.
    Transferable strategic utility15LinearModels and lessons reusable across decisions and cases.
    Mechanistic and causal depth12LinearIncentives, feedback, bottlenecks, constraints, and failure modes.
    Information density10QuadraticUseful learning per unit of reading: distinct facts, mechanisms, evidence and illuminating cases. Repeated frameworks are not padding when new cases add knowledge.
    Durability9LinearUsefulness beyond personalities, disputes, and hype.
    Direct domain fit7LinearFit to the scientific, industrial, and strategic interests in the repository.
    Expert authority5LinearScholarship, practice, access, and specialist scrutiny.
    Narrative architecture3LinearReadable, cumulative, memorable explanation.
    Authorial precision2LinearExact and disciplined prose.

    Quadratic contribution = x² / m
    Linear contribution = x
    Total = sum of ten contributions + T11 + T12 + H13 + P14 + O15

    Half attainment earns one quarter of the maximum on a quadratic criterion. Causal depth is linear, with maximum 12. Never square a total, deduction or already transformed contribution. When weights change, retain the assessed fraction of the old maximum unless new evidence warrants a changed assessment.

    Information density means useful learning

    Count the distinct facts, mechanisms, evidence, distinctions and cases learned for the reading required. Several examples of one idea can be highly educational: a shared framework does not make new history or a new boundary condition redundant. Shortness, difficult prose, jargon and topic appeal do not establish density. Deduct for material that adds little understanding, and assess the whole book.

    Attainment anchors: 9–10 sustained high learning yield with little removable material; 7–8 substantial learning with some lower-yield passages; 5–6 useful content mixed with substantial repetition or low-yield explanation; 3–4 a small payload spread over much of the book; 0–2 very little educational content for its length. These judgments are not ratios or measured facts per page. The quadratic contribution remains D²/10.

    The current focused review covers Why Nations Fail, The Righteous Mind and A Thousand Brains. Their evidence and confidence appear in Details. Other density values remain prior estimates and are marked as not recalibrated. Publisher descriptions alone cannot establish paragraph-level density; a full reading or representative text samples are stronger evidence. The exact rules below contain the assessment protocol.

    Apply five separate deductions

    • T11: 0 or −10. Deduct when the content predominantly covers racial history or civil movements, ecology or environmental issues, urban history, political or media celebrities, American-focused issues in both narrative and influence, American-tragedy themes, single-nation history or disease.
    • T12: 0 or −10. Deduct when war, military doctrine, politics or political intelligence, finance, media, power or philosophy is the central topic. These are welcome as applications or supporting domains around technology, energy, mathematics, physics, engineering, computing, logistics, resources, scaling, production, quality, invention and improvement.
    • H13: historical-topic age. For a clearly bounded historical subject, use the end of its central period: −min(12, max(0, review year − period end) / 25). Use fractional years, not completed blocks. An explicitly timeless or broad cross-period account with no single central period receives zero. Publication year is not a substitute for the topic endpoint.
    • P14: original publication age. −min(10, max(0, review year − original year) / 10). Reprints, translations and revised editions do not restart the clock. Record approximate composition dates for ancient works, with confidence. Use the first volume's original year for a nominated series.
    • O15: Amazon rating count. Use one matching product's total ratings: fewer than 10 → −20; 10–99 → −10; 100–999 → −5; at least 1,000 → 0. The bands do not add together.

    T11 and T12 are independent and can total −20. A thematic deduction and a veto test different conditions. The saved review year is 2026. Keep full precision for calculation, sorting and thresholds; display two decimals. Rounded displayed components can differ slightly from a displayed total.

    5. Record evidence and uncertainty

    Use publisher, author, library, primary-text and specialist-review evidence to establish identity, purpose, dates, claims and limitations. Publisher praise does not prove quality. Distinguish facts, interpretation and inference. Assign high, moderate or low confidence where supported; leave unknown facts unknown.

    Verify the title and author for Amazon observations. Total ratings are not written reviews. Do not sum editions or marketplaces. Record marketplace, product identifier, URL, retrieval date and snapshot limits. After unsuccessful retrieval attempts, an unavailable count remains unknown and uses the prescribed zero obscurity deduction. This fallback is not a claim that the book has zero ratings. Aggregator descriptions and reader counts require separate verification; the Books Guru capture contains mismatched descriptions.

    Record available reader aggregates from Book Marks, LibraryThing, StoryGraph, Goodreads and Amazon with attribution. Reader popularity is separate from the criterion assessment. Each source analysis contains the ranked eligible set, full criterion breakdowns, veto reasons, hard exclusions and remaining identity or access gaps.

    Page counts identify a particular edition, format, language, edition year and evidence source. A nominated series needs the complete set; partial volume counts are insufficient. Audio duration and ebook location counts are not pages. Source count measures distinct recorded source IDs, not independent endorsements.

    6. Assess domains and connections separately

    The model has 20 domains: science; mathematics and uncertainty; computing; high technology; engineering; energy; materials; production; quality and reliability; logistics; trade; scaling; innovation; institutions; economics; finance; politics and state capacity; military capability; strategy; and practical reasoning.

    Each domain uses a supported depth from 0 to 4, with rationale, references and confidence. An unassessed domain is unknown, not zero. These values supplement the 15-rule evaluation and start with no scoring weight.

    A connection records a specific causal or constraint mechanism involving two or more domains. Each participant needs a supported positive domain value and a distinct role. Record scope, strength, confidence and evidence. Strength progresses from a stated link (1), to developed causal steps (2), supported constraints or feedback (3), and a sustained, bounded explanation (4).

    Keep genuine mechanisms involving four, five or eight domains intact. Do not replace them with every possible pair or combine unrelated examples to inflate breadth. Join mechanisms only when evidence establishes a specific handoff or feedback within compatible scopes; a shared domain name is insufficient. Repeated mentions earn no connection bonus.

    An optional target specifies desired domains, depths, importance, connection strength and confidence. Coverage and weakest coverage measure depth. Connected strength selects the best supported connected explanation; connected domain count and joint-mechanism count distinguish a chain from a single joint mechanism. Integrated fit is LINK × (0.5 + 0.5 × FLOOR / 100). Partial reviews cannot establish exact final connection scores and remain unknown for those measures.

    7. Keep custom exploration separate

    The Books view starts with the repository's saved evaluation. Any variable can become an independent filter or score term. Normalization uses 0–100 or −100–100 in the controls, corresponding internally to 0–1 or −1–1. Signed weights, direct linear rates, quadratic curves, piecewise scaling and caps allow positive or negative contributions. Custom totals are not forced into 0–100.

    Filters move eligible books between two score-sorted lists. They do not turn a book into a repository exclusion or veto. Custom settings leave saved assessments and verdicts intact. Pareto axes can use variables or score combinations; dominance uses actual book points. Three boundaries are shown: the main frontier in red, a second in blue after removing every title on the first, and a third in dark yellow after removing both earlier layers. Tied titles leave together. Only matching books with known coordinates determine these boundaries. Curves are visual guides.

    Vetoed and excluded lists are read-only. Excluded books have no scores. Default book columns show year, pages, Amazon ratings and sources alongside score, title and author, selection, and Details. Additional raw values and scoring contributions are optional. The four controls stay above the results. Book details and calculations work offline; full source inputs and historical analyses open online.

    Exact repository instructions

    The complete instructions below are embedded from AGENTS.md when this HTML is built. They preserve the precise rules, examples, evidence requirements and output format behind this explanation.

    Read the complete repository rules
    This repo contains memory of continuous analysis and prioritisation of book recommendations found online.

The task of the agent it to digest the input link(s) and perform the analysis of the information available on that link page, which my include main information part and many auxiliary data and comments all of which should be considered.

File SOURCES.md contains a single table with the input links to be analysed, with the index in first column, date in second column, the link in third, and output analysis file name in forth.

File RECOMMENDED_BOOKS.md contains the main content of the repo, a single table of books recommended and amended after every analysis. First column is the date of entry, second is the the book publishing year, third is book author, then book title, then the score, and finaly the number of the source link as provided in the table in file SOURCES.md

File VETOED_BOOKS.md lists every currently vetoed source book once, with all contributing source numbers, the veto reason and confidence, and the full counterfactual criterion breakdown, thematic deduction, and total. Counterfactual scores suspend only the veto gate, retain the identified flaws, and do not make a book recommended. Hard-excluded books and non-book references belong in neither RECOMMENDED_BOOKS.md nor VETOED_BOOKS.md.

File EXCLUDED_BOOKS.md is the single cumulative list of hard-excluded source books under either exclusion rule. Add every future hard exclusion here once, identified by title and author when known. Use one alphabetized bullet per work, with no scores or rating columns. Put the exclusion reason and evidence in the relevant analysis; retain a short identity qualification in the list when needed to distinguish works. Do not add non-book references or titles absent from the source material. Check this file during every analysis, and reassess an earlier exclusion if new evidence changes the book's identity or eligibility. A book must appear in at most one of EXCLUDED_BOOKS.md, RECOMMENDED_BOOKS.md and VETOED_BOOKS.md. When its status changes, remove the obsolete entry and preserve prior analysis files as history.

Files analysis_<short-src>_<date> contains detailed output of every specific analysis of the source. For every input link it should provide an overview of the thinking process, final recommended set with the details of the scoring, and other useful or extreme info such as which books were the worst and especially unfitting to be recommended. Majority of the format detail is part of the main analysis prompt. "short-src" is short readable abriviation of input source link text up to 12 characters so make it specific and context relevant, and date uses YYMMDD_HHMM: a two-digit year, month, day, underscore, hour and minute, with no T, seconds or timezone suffix. Use Europe/Warsaw local time. Store analysis files in the analysis/ folder. The full path is analysis/analysis_<short-src>_YYMMDD_HHMM.md.

Main analysis guidelines are below. They are to be an input for every analysis and provide detailed instructions on collecting, filtering, scoring, judging, and formatting the final result. This prompt is the most relevant part of this page and use is in its strict form and prescribed detail with almost mathematical rigor.

# THE ANALYSIS PROMPT
Study the thread at the link, including all the individual post's comments which contain most of the data: [INPUT]

Fully utilize the main section, all the comments, and every other information available on the page as the only source of the list of titles for the analysis ahead. Make sure to use any technique to fully expand the comments section to collect all comments and subcomments thus extracting any possibly useful information.

Score every source book that passes the hard exclusions and is not vetoed, and include it in the analysis, the final ranked recommendation table, and RECOMMENDED_BOOKS.md. Provide each book's full criterion breakdown, applicable thematic deduction, total score, and verdict. Poor topic fit or a low score is not an additional exclusion rule; uncertain assessments remain included with an explicit confidence level.

Reevaluate every eligible book encountered in a source, even if it already appears in RECOMMENDED_BOOKS.md or previous analyses. Read the relevant prior analyses and reassess the veto decision, every scoring criterion, thematic deduction, verdict, and confidence using both prior and new evidence. Resolve conflicts and correct earlier errors; do not merely reuse or average old scores, or count repeated mentions as independent evidence of quality. In the new analysis, cite the contributing sources and prior analyses and explain why the final score and conclusion changed or stayed the same. Update the existing RECOMMENDED_BOOKS.md entry rather than adding a duplicate, retaining all contributing source numbers; remove it from RECOMMENDED_BOOKS.md if now vetoed. Preserve prior analysis files as history.

Prioritize pragmatic intellectual non-fiction titles on how society, economy, science, finance, geostrategy, strategic, technology, history of civilization, power, trade, industrialization, logistics, scaling and hyperscaling in sense of either miniaturization or globalization or speed or power, prosperity, and military, policy-making all interconnect and work; both the mechanisms and the utility.

Take into account I'm theoretical physicist specializing in QFT, particle and cosmology, computation and numerical simulation, so I find popular physics books less attractive, but at the same time have inclination towards specific topics almost stereotypical for theoretical physicists like strategic considerations, quantification (physical, financial, risk, strategic estimates), modeling any or all aspects of the world, effective (fast, cheap, accurate) heuristical thinking, technological leverage, scaling of logistics or technology, deeply coherent argumentation, pragmatic aspects of philosophy of all aspects of living, memorable anecdotes with strong generalizable principles, knowledge as a tool, etc...

I'm NOT interested in dry administration, particularly isolated historical notes without wider context or ultimate influence, focus on sports or politics or media celebrity, hyped buzzwords, pathological or demagogue political tactic, ideological extremes, any form of fanaticism, self-help, how-to-get-rich-quick advices, self-centered agendas, conspiracies, supernatural, Vietnam war or "american tragedy" rethorics, ecology or environment topics, history of slavery or afro-american racial or civil or other minority issues, american civil or urban history, single nation history, disease.

Make elaborate use of any external or built-in resource to accurately resolve the criteria below.

## Hard exclusion rules - a book is excluded and not even considered vetoed:
1. Works which do not represent a book and are never published in a book form.
2. Exclude fiction books and do not consider them vetoed. Discard them before scoring or further analysis.
3. Technical training and reference exclusion. Exclude works whose main purpose is to teach a technical curriculum, develop specialist proficiency, present formal proofs or derivations, provide procedures, or serve as a technical reference. Clear prose, historical introductions, conceptual explanations, prestige, and absence of exercises do not override this exclusion. Allow technically demanding books when their main purpose is sustained explanation of discoveries, mechanisms, decisions, or historical development, and their main intellectual value can be obtained without completing a course of technical study. Historical scientific treatises remain excluded when their main content requires reconstruction of specialist proofs, notation, or obsolete technical methods. Historical importance alone does not establish eligibility. Historical surveys and annotated chronologies can qualify when substantive explanatory prose provides value beyond locating references.

Apply both hard exclusions before vetoes or scoring, including to profile examples and books previously recommended or vetoed. Scores, reader ratings, author standing and the biography exceptions under V3 cannot override a hard exclusion. Record hard-excluded books in EXCLUDED_BOOKS.md, not in either scored book list, and do not assign them new scores or counterfactual veto scores.

## Veto rules - a book is excluded regardless of score when one of these is present at a serious level:
1. Epistemic failure - The central argument depends on material factual errors, distorted sources, invalid causal inference, concealed uncertainty, or obsolete information presented as current. 
2. Ideological capture - The argument depends on political, religious, national, cultural, or economic allegiance rather than evidence. Counterexamples are ignored, caricatured, or explained away asymmetrically. 
3. No transferable intellectual payload - After removing names, dates, personalities, and local detail, little remains in the form of mechanisms, constraints, models, heuristics, or generalizable lessons. Exceptions are mathematical, science or high-tech biographies or memoires like Skunk Works, "The man from the future" about von Neumann, "The man who solved the market" about Simons, "Never at rest" about Newton, etc...
4. Hype or ephemerality dependence - The book’s value depends primarily on a passing controversy, fashionable terminology, launch publicity, or premature claims of revolutionary importance. Educated speculative prediction is allowed if stated in professional substantiated balanced argumentative way with elaborate guardrails.
5. Religious doctrine or ideological extremism. Veto scripture, devotional or proselytizing works, and works whose central purpose is to establish religious doctrine as authoritative truth. Also veto explicit advocacy of ideological extremism, supported by specific evidence such as dehumanization, persecution, violent domination or suppression of dissent. A manifesto label, advocacy, activism, political position, technological vision, institutional criticism or proposed reform is not sufficient. Historical or analytical discussion of religion or extremist movements is not itself advocacy.
6. Partisan mobilization. Veto works whose dominant purpose is to recruit, rally, or reinforce allegiance to a political leader, party, or movement, or to supply campaign attacks against opponents. Establish this purpose from the introduction, representative passages, and stated aims. Apply the rule equally across political positions. A policy conclusion, institutional criticism, or reform proposal alone is insufficient.

## Scoring rules:
%  Rule  Weight  Operational question
1. Evidence and inferential integrity 20-quadratic Are the important claims well sourced, factually reliable, logically connected, and explicit about uncertainty and counterevidence?
2. Systems integration 17-quadratic Does it coherently connect several relevant layers: science, engineering, production, trade, finance, institutions, geography, military power, state capacity or culture?
3. Transferable strategic utility 15 Can its insights be reused in other industries, institutions, technologies, historical cases or strategic decisions?
4. Mechanistic and causal depth 12 Does the book explain how the system works—feedback loops, incentives, bottlenecks, constraints, failure modes and causal chains—or merely report events?
5. Information density and length justification 10-quadratic Does each chapter materially advance evidence, mechanism or interpretation? Is the book’s length earned rather than padded?
6. Durability and resistance to hype 9 Will the book remain useful after current personalities, policy disputes and news cycles have passed?
7. Direct domain fit 7 Does it substantially illuminate physics, mathematics, computing, high-tech utility, technology, industry, infrastructure, trade, geostrategy, scientific organization, institutional power or strategic risk?
8. Expert authority and intellectual standing 5 Has it survived serious specialist attention? Is the author authoritative through scholarship, access, practice or unusual synthesis?
9. Narrative architecture and clarity 3 Is the structure readable, cumulative and memorable without converting ambiguity into theatrical certainty?
10. Authorial precision and finesse 2 Is the prose exact, controlled and conceptually disciplined?
11. Thematic negative points -10 Does the book content predominantly cover racial history or civil movement, ecology or environmental issues, urban history, political figure or media celebrity, American-focused issues in both narrative and influence, American tragedy topic, single nation history, disease?
12. Thematic negative points -10 if central topic is war, military doctrine, politics or political inteligence, finance, media, power, philosophy. These are allowed even expected as auxiliary or application domains, with central expected to be technology, energy, mathematics, physics, engineering, computing, logistics, resource management, scaling, production, industrial quality & reliability & precision, industrial inteligence, invention & innovation, improvement in the most broad sense. Example of great thematic balance is Skunk Works. Use this rule separately in addition to rule 11.
13. Thematic recency negative points -1 per 25 years of age of the central topic of the book if book covers some specific time period referencing the end of that period, maximally up to -12 points. Example of great historic balance is Why Nations Fail. Apply when the book is clearly about some historic period, ignore otherwise.
14. Publishing recency negative points -1 for every 10 years of book original production age, maximally up to -10 points.
15. Obscurity negative points -X if book has less than Y Amazon ratings: (20, 10) (10, 100) (5, 1000). Use when count is available, ignore otherwise.

### Assessing information density and length justification

Judge useful learning per unit of reading, not brevity, jargon, difficulty, or the number of headline theses. Count distinct explanatory facts, mechanisms, distinctions, evidence and illuminating cases. A new example of an existing framework earns credit when it adds historical knowledge, a different constraint, a comparison, a boundary condition or a useful application. Repetition is a deduction only when it adds little understanding. Do not treat a repeated framework as proof of padding, or a short book as proof of density.

Use the same anchored 0–10 attainment scale across topics: 9–10 sustained high learning yield with little removable material; 7–8 substantial learning with some recap or lower-yield stretches; 5–6 useful content mixed with substantial low-yield explanation or repetition; 3–4 a small payload spread over much of the book; 0–2 very little educational content for its length. Half-points may express an intermediate judgment, not measurement precision. Assess the whole book rather than only its strongest section. Distinguish educational examples from anecdotes that only restate the claim. Keep factual reliability under E, causal depth under M, clarity under N and topic preference under F; do not deduct the same concern again under D without a separate density reason.

Record the evidence inspected (full text, named sample chapters, contents, independent review, or reader report), examples of added learning and any identified low-yield material. Contents and publisher blurbs alone cannot establish paragraph-level density. Use high confidence only for broad direct text coverage; samples and corroborating reviews usually support moderate confidence, and description-only estimates are low confidence. Personal reading reports are relevant evidence but not objective measurements. The 0–10 ratings are judgments, not a ratio scale: 8 is not twice the information of 4. Retain prior estimates outside the reviewed set and label them as not yet recalibrated; do not claim a catalog-wide density audit from a few examples.

### Scoring calculation

Each maximum above is the maximum number of points that criterion can contribute. First assess the criterion's attainment as linear points `x` from 0 to its own maximum `m`.

- Apply a quadratic profile **only** to evidence and inferential integrity (`m = 20`), systems integration (`m = 17`), and information density and length justification (`m = 10`): `points = m × (x / m)^2 = x^2 / m`.
- All seven other positive criteria remain linear: `points = x`. Mechanistic and causal depth has a maximum of **12** and is **not quadratic**.
- Use the criterion's own maximum as the denominator, not a common 10-point scale. Zero attainment gives 0 points; full attainment gives the full maximum. Half attainment gives one quarter of the maximum on a quadratic criterion.
- Sum the ten resulting contributions, then apply rules 11–15 separately: `total = sum(points) + T11 + T12 + H13 + P14 + O15`. Each thematic deduction is 0 or −10; both can apply, for a combined −20. The positive maxima sum to 100. Do not square the total or any deduction.
- For rule 13, use the end of the central historical period: `H13 = -min(12, max(0, review_year - period_end_year) / 25)`. Use fractional points, not completed 25-year blocks. A timeless argument or broad cross-period account with no single central period receives 0. Publication age is not a substitute for topic age. Record the assessed endpoint and its confidence.
- For rule 14, use original publication age: `P14 = -min(10, max(0, review_year - original_year) / 10)`. Use fractional points, capped at a maximum deduction of 10 points. Reprints, translations and revised editions do not reset the original year. For ancient works, use an explicitly recorded approximate composition or compilation year and its confidence. For a nominated series, use its first volume's original year.
- For rule 15, use one matching Amazon product's rating aggregate, without adding counts across editions or marketplaces: fewer than 10 → −20; 10–99 → −10; 100–999 → −5; at least 1,000 → 0. These bands are mutually exclusive. Verify the title and author, distinguish total ratings from written reviews, and record the marketplace, product identifier, URL, retrieval date and any snapshot limitation. An unavailable count is unknown, not zero; after retrieval attempts, apply the specified fallback of no obscurity deduction and label that fallback.
- Do not output provisional range, but single numerical score per book. Use prescribed fallbacks if needed.
- Retain unrounded values for calculation, sorting and verdict thresholds. Display criterion contributions and totals to two decimal places. A displayed total can differ slightly from the sum of displayed components because components are rounded separately.
- When migrating an earlier linear assessment with an old maximum `m_old`, preserve its assessed attainment unless new evidence warrants a change: `x_new = m_new × (x_old / m_old)`. Then apply the current profile once. Thus an old systems-integration score `S` out of 12 becomes `17 × (S / 12)^2`, and an old causal-depth score `M` out of 17 becomes `12 × (M / 17)`. Keep the underlying linear assessment and the final contribution separate so a later update cannot apply the quadratic curve twice.

Use criterion names as the identity when an order or weight changes. In existing ledgers, `S` means systems integration and `M` means mechanistic and causal depth; do not swap their meanings. A scoring-profile change alone does not change a hard exclusion, veto, thematic classification, or confidence in the book-level evidence.
